Package com.j3d.engine.interact.input.mouse

Class SnapMouseOwner

java.lang.Object
java.awt.event.MouseAdapter
com.j3d.engine.interact.input.mouse.MouseOwner
com.j3d.engine.interact.input.mouse.SnapMouseOwner
All Implemented Interfaces:
EventEmitterInterface, MouseListener, MouseMotionListener, MouseWheelListener, EventListener
Direct Known Subclasses:
TransformMouseOwner
public class SnapMouseOwner extends MouseOwner
A MouseOwner which enables child classes which extend it, the capability to snap to GObjects.

This class:

  • Detects nearby GObjects (points and midpoints of lines) within a small radius of the mouse cursor.
  • Highlights these potential snap targets visually in the scene.
  • Broadcasts a EventType.SNAP_TO_OBJ event when the user right-clicks on a highlighted snap target.
Subclasses can extend this to enable snapping behaviour for their specific mouse interactions, such as transforming objects to align with other objects in the scene.
Author:
Lehlogonolo Poole

    • consumer

      private Consumer<Graphics2D> consumer()
      Returns a Consumer<Graphics2D> that handles the visual representation of snapping candidates. This consumer is scheduled with the SceneManager to draw overlays, identifying and highlighting potential snap targets (points and midpoints of lines) within the snapping region.
      Returns:
      A Consumer that draws the snapping overlays.

    • mouseMoved

      public void mouseMoved(MouseEvent e)
      Handles mouse movement events. When the mouse moves, it updates the mouseLoc, clears previous snapping candidates, and queries the SelectionManager for new potential snap targets within the snapping region. It also schedules the overlap consumer if not already scheduled.
      Specified by:
      mouseMoved in interface MouseMotionListener
      Overrides:
      mouseMoved in class MouseOwner
      Parameters:
      e - The MouseEvent generated by the mouse movement.

    • clear

      public void clear()
      Clears all snapping-related state, including removing the overlap consumer from the SceneManager, clearing snapping candidates, and resetting the hoveringOver object. This should be called when snapping is no longer needed.
